**Finding: compliant** (rule GOVLAW, no redline)

Section 28 lands squarely on our preferred position:

- **§ 28.1** — governed by the laws of the State of New York, with CISG expressly disclaimed.
- **§ 28.2** — exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, with mutual submission to personal jurisdiction and waiver of venue/forum objections.
- **No arbitration** — a document-wide search for "arbitration" returned zero hits, so the walk-away risk flagged in the planner hint (English or offshore law with a foreign-seated arbitration, given Brightline is a UK Ltd.) does not materialize.

Two ancillary points noted but not flagged:
- The § 28.2 carve-out allowing either party to seek temporary injunctive relief elsewhere is mutual and limited to confidential information and IP; it does not displace the exclusive court venue.
- The § 28.3 pre-filing executive escalation (15 business days) expressly does not delay urgent relief or filings needed to preserve a limitations period, so it is not an access-to-court barrier.

Section 29 (notices) is consistent and creates no service-of-process conflict with the venue clause.
